name: Saint John Baptist de La Salle
history: A wealthy canon of Reims who gave up his position and his fortune to train teachers for the children of the poor. He founded the Brothers of the Christian Schools, taught in French rather than Latin, grouped pupils in classes and opened some of the first colleges for teachers. Pius XII named him patron of teachers.
life: Jean-Baptiste de La Salle was the eldest son of a noble family of Reims, a canon of the cathedral at sixteen and a priest at twenty-seven. In 1679 he met Adrien Nyel, who wanted to open free schools for poor boys, and helped him find teachers. Seeing how unprepared they were, he took them into his own house to live and pray with him, to the dismay of his family. He resigned his canonry and, in the famine of 1684, gave away his inheritance to the hungry, so that he would stand with his teachers in poverty. From them grew the Brothers of the Christian Schools, religious who were not priests and gave their lives to teaching. He met fierce opposition, lawsuits from the writing masters and conflict within his own institute, and went through periods of deep discouragement. He died at Rouen on Good Friday, 7 April 1719.
prayerTo: Saint John Baptist de La Salle, you gave up wealth and honour so that poor children might learn and know God. Pray for teachers, for all who form the young, and for children who have no one to teach them. Help me to remember that I stand always in the holy presence of God. Amen.
penance: Thank a teacher who formed you, or give to a school or charity that educates poor children. Make the Lasallian pause: stop several times today and remember you are in God’s presence.
meditation: Every lesson in his schools began with the words: let us remember that we are in the holy presence of God. Where do you most forget it?
